sentences.zh: 陳修，字伯昂，上饒人。

translations.literal: Chen Xiu, styled Bo'ang, was a native of Shangrao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xiu, courtesy name Bo'ang, was from Shangrao.

sentences.zh: 從太祖平浙東，授理官。

translations.literal: He followed the Taizu Emperor in pacifying eastern Zhejiang and was appointed a judicial official.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the founding emperor in pacifying eastern Zhejiang and was appointed a judicial officer.

sentences.zh: 援引律令，悉本寬厚，盡改元季弊政。

translations.literal: In citing statutes and ordinances he took leniency as his basis throughout and wholly reformed the abuses of the Yuan season.
translations.idiomatic: In applying the law he consistently favored leniency and swept away the corrupt practices of the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 擢兵部郎中，遷濟南知府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director in the Ministry of War and transferred to be prefect of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Ministry of War, then transferred to serve as prefect of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 時亂後，比戶彫殘，且多衛將練兵屯田其間。

translations.literal: At the time, after the turmoil, household after household was devastated, and moreover many guard generals drilled troops and opened military colonies there.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of war the populace lay in ruins, and many guard officers drilled troops and opened military colonies in the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 修撫治有方，兵民相安，流亡復業。

translations.literal: Xiu governed with effective measures; soldiers and civilians lived in peace, and exiles returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Chen governed with skill; soldiers and civilians lived at peace, and refugees returned to their fields.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his work.

sentences.zh: 六部初屬中書省，權輕，多仰承丞相意指。

translations.literal: At first the Six Ministries were subordinate to the Central Secretariat; their authority was slight, and they largely deferred to the chief councillor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the Six Ministries answered to the Central Secretariat, held little power, and largely followed the chief councillor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 毅、修及詹同、吳琳、趙好德輩，居吏部稱賢，然亦無大建豎。

translations.literal: Yi, Xiu, and Zhan Tong, Wu Lin, Zhao Haode, and their like, while serving in the Ministry of Personnel were called worthy, yet they likewise achieved no great accomplishments.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Yi, Chen Xiu, Zhan Tong, Wu Lin, Zhao Haode, and others were regarded as capable ministers of personnel, yet none left a major mark.

sentences.zh: 至十三年，中書省革，部權乃專，而銓衡為尤要。

translations.literal: By the thirteenth year the Central Secretariat was abolished; ministerial authority then stood alone, and the power of appointment and assessment became especially vital.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Central Secretariat was abolished, the ministries gained full authority, and control over appointments became paramount.

sentences.zh: 顧帝用法嚴，熂以排宋訥誅，善貶，澤拜尚書。

translations.literal: Yet the Emperor applied the law severely: Xi was executed for opposing Song Ne, Shan was demoted, and Ze was appointed Minister.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor enforced the law harshly: Xi Yu was executed for opposing Song Ne, Zhai Shan was demoted, and Li Ze was appointed minister.

sentences.zh: 未數月罷。

translations.literal: Within a few months he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 惟信曆侍郎，拜尚書，幾二載，卒於官雲。

translations.literal: Wei Xin had served as Vice Minister, was appointed Minister, served for nearly two years, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xin had risen through the vice-ministership to the ministry itself, held the post for nearly two years, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 趙好德，字秉彝，汝陽人。

translations.literal: Zhao Haode, styled Bingyi, was a native of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Haode, courtesy name Bingyi, was from Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 由安慶知府入為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: From prefect of Anqing he entered the capital as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court from the prefecture of Anqing as vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 進尚書，改吏部。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Minister and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其典銓平，嘗召與四輔官入內殿。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his even-handed conduct of appointments and once summoned him with the four chief assisting officials into the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his impartial management of appointments and once summoned him with the four chief counselors to the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 坐論治道，命畫史圖像禁中。

translations.literal: Seated, they discussed the way of governance, and he was ordered to have court painters portray their likenesses within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: They sat discussing statecraft, and the emperor had court painters record their likenesses in the palace.

sentences.zh: 終陝西參政。

translations.literal: He ended his career as administrative commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as administrative commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 子毅，永樂中，官至工部侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Yi, in the Yongle reign, reached the post of Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi rose under the Yongle emperor to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 翟善，字敬夫，以貢舉曆官吏部文選司主事。

translations.literal: Zhai Shan, styled Jingfu, through presentation as a tribute student rose through offices to chief clerk of the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Shan, courtesy name Jingfu, entered service through the tribute-student route and rose to chief clerk in the Ministry of Personnel's appointments bureau.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，尚書詹徽、侍郎傅友文誅，命善署部事，再遷至尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when Ministers Zhan Hui and Vice Minister Fu Youwen were executed, Shan was ordered to handle ministry affairs and was again promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, after Ministers Zhan Hui and Fu Youwen were executed, Shan was placed in charge of the ministry and soon promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 明於經術，奏對合帝意。

translations.literal: He was clear in classical learning; his memorials and replies accorded with the Emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Well versed in the classics, he pleased the emperor in memorials and audience.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善雖年少，氣宇恢廓，他人莫及也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Though Shan is young, his bearing is broad and open; others cannot match him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Shan is young, yet his spirit is expansive; none can equal him."

sentences.zh: 」欲為營第於鄉，善辭。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to build him a mansion in his home district; Shan declined.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor offered to build him a mansion in his home district, Shan declined.

sentences.zh: 又欲除其家戍籍，善曰：「戍卒宜增，豈可以臣破例。

translations.literal: The Emperor also wished to remove his family's garrison registration. Shan said, "Garrison soldiers ought to be increased; how can a subject break precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also wished to exempt his family from corvée garrison duty. Shan replied, "We need more garrison soldiers, not fewer; a minister must not bend the rule for himself."

sentences.zh: 」帝益以為賢。

translations.literal: The Emperor esteemed him all the more as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 二十八年坐事，降宣化知縣以終。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was implicated in an affair, demoted to magistrate of Xuanhua, and ended his days there.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was punished for an offense, demoted to magistrate of Xuanhua, and ended his career there.

sentences.zh: 李仁，唐縣人。

translations.literal: Li Ren was a native of Tang County.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ren was from Tang County.

sentences.zh: 初仕陳友諒。

translations.literal: At first he served Chen Youliang.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Chen Youliang.

sentences.zh: 王師克武昌，來歸。

translations.literal: When the royal army took Wuchang, he came over in submission.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army captured Wuchang, he submitted.

sentences.zh: 以常遇春薦，代陶安知黃州府。

translations.literal: On Chang Yuchun's recommendation he replaced Tao An as prefect of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Chang Yuchun, he replaced Tao An as prefect of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 曆官侍郎，進尚書。

translations.literal: He passed through the vice-ministership and was advanced to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the vice-ministership to minister.

sentences.zh: 坐事謫青州，政最。

translations.literal: Implicated in an affair, he was banished to Qingzhou, where his administration ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for an offense, he was sent to Qingzhou, where his governance ranked first.

sentences.zh: 擢戶部侍郎，致仕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of revenue and then retired.

sentences.zh: 吳琳，黃崗人。

translations.literal: Wu Lin was a native of Huanggang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lin was from Huanggang.

sentences.zh: 太祖下武昌，以詹同薦，召為國子助教。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor took Wuchang, on Zhan Tong's recommendation he was summoned as an assistant instructor at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: After the founding emperor took Wuchang, Zhan Tong recommended him, and he was summoned as an assistant instructor at the National University.

sentences.zh: 經術逾於同。

translations.literal: His mastery of the classics surpassed Tong's.
translations.idiomatic: His command of the classics surpassed Zhan Tong's.

sentences.zh: 吳元年除浙江按察司僉事，復入為起居注。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wu he was appointed investigating censor of Zhejiang; he later re-entered court as recorder of the ruler's movements.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wu he was made investigating censor of Zhejiang, then returned to court as recorder of the ruler's movements.

sentences.zh: 命齎幣帛求書于四方。

translations.literal: He was ordered to carry silks and gifts to seek books from all quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent with gifts to seek books throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 洪武六年，自兵部尚書改吏部，嘗與同迭主部事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongwu he was transferred from Minister of War to Minister of Personnel and once shared charge of the ministry with Tong in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year six he moved from the Ministry of War to the Ministry of Personnel and at times shared its leadership with Zhan Tong in rotation.

sentences.zh: 逾年，乞歸。

translations.literal: After more than a year he requested to return home.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he asked to retire home.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗遣使察之。

translations.literal: The Emperor once sent an envoy to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once sent an envoy to look in on him.

sentences.zh: 使者潛至旁舍，一農人坐小杌，起拔稻苗布田，貌甚端謹。

translations.literal: The envoy stole to a neighboring cottage, where a farmer sat on a low stool, rose to pull rice seedlings and set them in the field, his bearing very proper and careful.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy slipped to a neighboring cottage and saw a farmer on a low stool rise to transplant rice; his manner was grave and careful.

sentences.zh: 使者前曰：「此有吳尚書者，在否？

translations.literal: The envoy stepped forward and said, "Is there a former Minister Wu here?"
translations.idiomatic: The envoy stepped forward and asked, "Is former Minister Wu here?"

sentences.zh: 」農人斂手，對曰：「琳是也。

translations.literal: The farmer folded his hands and replied, "I am Lin."
translations.idiomatic: The farmer bowed and answered, "I am Lin."

sentences.zh: 」使者以狀聞。

translations.literal: The envoy reported the circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy reported what he had seen.

sentences.zh: 帝為嘉歎。

translations.literal: The Emperor commended and sighed over it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him with admiration.

sentences.zh: 楊思義，不詳其籍裏。

translations.literal: Yang Siyi — his native place is not recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Siyi — his place of origin is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 太祖稱吳王，授起居注。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor styled himself Prince of Wu, he was appointed recorder of the ruler's movements.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor took the title Prince of Wu, he was made recorder of the ruler's movements.

sentences.zh: 初，錢谷隸中書省。

translations.literal: At first fiscal revenues were subordinate to the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At first fiscal affairs belonged to the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 吳元年始設司農卿，以思義為之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wu the office of Director of Agriculture was first established, with Siyi appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wu the Directorate of Agriculture was created, with Siyi at its head.

sentences.zh: 明年設六部，改為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year the Six Ministries were established, and he was changed to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Six Ministries were formed, and he became minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 大亂之後，人多廢業。

translations.literal: After the great turmoil many people had abandoned their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars many people had abandoned their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 思義請令民間皆植桑麻，四年始征其稅。

translations.literal: Siyi requested that all households plant mulberry and hemp, with taxation to begin only after four years.
translations.idiomatic: Siyi proposed that every household plant mulberry and hemp, with taxes levied only after four years.

sentences.zh: 不種桑者輸絹，不種麻者輸布，如《周官》裏布法。

translations.literal: Those who did not plant mulberry were to pay silk; those who did not plant hemp were to pay cloth — as in the district-cloth method of the "Offices of Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: Households without mulberry paid silk instead; those without hemp paid cloth — following the district-cloth levy of the "Rites of Zhou."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 帝念水旱不時，緩急無所恃，命思義令天下立預備倉，以防水旱。

translations.literal: The Emperor, mindful that flood and drought came untimely and that in urgent need there was nothing to rely on, ordered Siyi to have the empire establish reserve granaries against flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that floods and droughts came without warning and left no reserve in times of need, the emperor ordered Siyi to establish granaries throughout the realm against famine.

sentences.zh: 思義首邦計，以農桑積貯為急。

translations.literal: Siyi put state finance first and took agriculture, sericulture, and storage as urgent priorities.
translations.idiomatic: Siyi put state finance first and made farming, sericulture, and grain reserves his chief concerns.

sentences.zh: 凡所興設，雖本帝意，而經畫詳密，時稱其能。

translations.literal: All institutions he launched, though rooted in the Emperor's intent, were planned in close detail, and at the time he was praised for his capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Though each measure followed the emperor's intent, Siyi planned them in meticulous detail, and contemporaries praised his ability.

sentences.zh: 調陝西行省參政，卒於官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be administrative commissioner of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administrative commissioner of Shaanxi and died in office.

sentences.zh: 終洪武朝，為戶部尚書者四十余人，皆不久於職，績用罕著。

translations.literal: Through the entire Hongwu reign more than forty men served as Minister of Revenue, yet none long held office, and their achievements were rarely notable.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Hongwu reign more than forty men held the ministry of revenue, yet few lasted long or left a notable record.

sentences.zh: 惟茹太素、楊靖、滕德懋、范敏、費震之屬，差有聲。

translations.literal: Only Ru Taisu, Yang Jing, Teng Demao, Fan Min, Fei Zhen, and their like had some reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ru Taisu, Yang Jing, Teng Demao, Fan Min, Fei Zhen, and a few others enjoyed any real renown.

sentences.zh: 太素、靖自有傳。

translations.literal: Taisu and Jing have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Taisu and Jing have biographies of their own.

sentences.zh: 德懋，字思勉，吳人。

translations.literal: Demao, styled Simian, was a native of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Demao, courtesy name Simian, was from Wu.

sentences.zh: 由中書省掾曆外任。

translations.literal: From a clerkship in the Central Secretariat he passed through posts outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from a clerkship in the Central Secretariat through provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，召拜兵部尚書，尋改戶部。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was summoned and appointed Minister of War, soon transferred to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year three he was summoned as minister of war, then moved to revenue.

sentences.zh: 為人有才辨，器量弘偉。

translations.literal: As a man he was talented and quick in debate, with a broad and lofty bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-witted and eloquent, with a broad and generous spirit.

sentences.zh: 長於奏疏，一時招徠詔諭之文，多出其手。

translations.literal: He excelled at memorials; for a time most documents of recruitment and imperial instruction came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at memorials, and for a time most edicts of recruitment and reassurance bore his pen.

sentences.zh: 以事免官，卒。

translations.literal: Implicated in an affair, he was dismissed from office and died.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for an offense, he was dismissed and later died.

sentences.zh: 範敏，閿鄉人。

translations.literal: Fan Min was a native of Lüxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Min was from Lüxiang.

sentences.zh: 洪武八年舉秀才，擢戶部郎中。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Hongwu he was raised as a xiucai and promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year eight he passed the xiucai examination and was made director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十三年授試尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was given trial appointment as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was appointed acting minister.

sentences.zh: 薦耆儒王本等，皆拜四輔官。

translations.literal: He recommended venerable scholars such as Wang Ben, all of whom were appointed to the four chief assisting offices.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended senior scholars such as Wang Ben, all of whom became the four chief counselors.

sentences.zh: 帝以徭役不均，命編造黃冊。

translations.literal: Because corvée labor was uneven, the Emperor ordered the compilation of the yellow registers.
translations.idiomatic: Finding corvée duties unevenly assigned, the emperor ordered the compilation of the yellow registers.

sentences.zh: 敏議：百一十戶為裏，丁多者十人為裏長，鳩一里之事以供歲役。

translations.literal: Min proposed: one hundred and ten households formed a li; where adult males were numerous, ten men served as li head and gathered the li's affairs to supply the year's corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Min proposed grouping 110 households into a li, with ten adult males as li head to organize the community's annual corvée.

sentences.zh: 十年一周。

translations.literal: The rotation ran in a ten-year cycle.
translations.idiomatic: The rotation completed a ten-year cycle.

sentences.zh: 餘百戶為十甲。

translations.literal: The remaining hundred households were divided into ten jia.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining hundred households were divided into ten jia units.

sentences.zh: 後遂仍其制不廢。

translations.literal: Later the system was retained and not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The system was later retained and never abolished.

sentences.zh: 明年以不職罷。

translations.literal: The next year he was dismissed for incompetence in office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was dismissed for incompetence.

sentences.zh: 費震，鄱陽人。

translations.literal: Fei Zhen was a native of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Zhen was from Poyang.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，以賢良征，為吉水知州，寬惠得民，擢知漢中。

translations.literal: In early Hongwu he was summoned as a worthy and able man, served as prefect of Jishui with leniency and kindness that won the people, and was promoted to prefect of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In early Hongwu he was summoned as a worthy man, governed Jishui with leniency that won the people, and was promoted to prefect of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 歲凶盜起，發倉粟十余萬斛貸民，俾秋成還倉。

translations.literal: In a year of famine bandits rose; he released more than a hundred thousand piculs from the granary to lend the people, to be returned to the granary after the autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: When famine brought banditry, he lent the people more than a hundred thousand piculs from the granary to be repaid after harvest.

sentences.zh: 盜聞，皆來歸。

translations.literal: When bandits heard of it, they all came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, the bandits submitted.

sentences.zh: 令占宅自為保伍，得數千家。

translations.literal: He ordered them to occupy dwellings and form mutual-security groups of their own, gathering several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He had them settle in homes and organize themselves into mutual-security groups, numbering several thousand households.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and commended it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and praised his work.

sentences.zh: 後坐事被逮，以有善政，特釋為寶鈔提舉。

translations.literal: Later, implicated in an affair, he was arrested; because of his good administration he was specially released and made superintendent of treasure notes.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was arrested for an offense, but because of his good record he was released and made superintendent of paper currency.

sentences.zh: 十一年，帝謂吏部曰：「資格為常流設耳，有才能者當不次用之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Emperor said to the Ministry of Personnel, "Seniority ranks are set up for the ordinary stream; men of talent ought to be employed out of turn."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the emperor told the Ministry of Personnel, "Seniority is for ordinary men; the capable should be promoted without waiting their turn."

sentences.zh: 」超擢者九十五人。

translations.literal: "Ninety-five persons were exceptionally promoted."
translations.idiomatic: "Ninety-five were promoted out of turn."

sentences.zh: 而拜震戶部侍郎，尋進尚書。

translations.literal: And Zhen was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue, soon advanced to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Among them Fei Zhen was made vice minister of revenue and soon promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 奉命定丞相、御史大夫以下負祿之制。

translations.literal: He received orders to fix the stipend system for the chancellor, censor-in-chief, and all ranks below.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial orders he set salary scales for the chancellor, the censor-in-chief, and officials beneath them.

sentences.zh: 出為湖廣布政使，以老致仕。

translations.literal: He went out as Huguang administrative commissioner and retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Huguang administrative commissioner and retired when old.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，有張琬者，鄱陽人。

translations.literal: In early Hongwu there was one Zhang Wan, a native of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongwu there was Zhang Wan of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 以貢士試高等，授給事中，改戶部主事。

translations.literal: Having passed the tribute-scholar examination in the upper grade, he was appointed supervising secretary, then transferred to principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He placed high in the tribute-scholar examination, became a supervising secretary, and was then transferred to a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝問天下財賦、戶口之數。

translations.literal: One day the Emperor asked the figures for the empire's revenue and taxes and its household population.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor asked him for the empire's revenue and population totals.

sentences.zh: 口對無遺。

translations.literal: He answered orally without omission.
translations.idiomatic: He recited them flawlessly from memory.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，立擢左侍郎。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and immediately promoted him to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor promptly promoted him to left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 謹身殿災，上言時政。

translations.literal: When the Hall of Cultivating the Body burned, he submitted a memorial on current policy.
translations.idiomatic: After fire struck the Hall of Cultivating the Body, he memorialized on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，請蠲民租百萬余石。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he requested remission of more than a million piculs of the people's land tax.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine he urged remitting over a million piculs of land tax.

sentences.zh: 俱見嘉納。

translations.literal: All were seen and commended and adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 琬才敏，有心計，年二十七，卒於官。

translations.literal: Wan was talented and quick, with schemes in mind; at age twenty-seven he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wan was clever and resourceful; he died in office at twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 時人惜之。

translations.literal: Men of the time lamented it.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries mourned his early death.

sentences.zh: 周禎，字文典，江寧人。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhen, style name Wendian, was a native of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhen (Wendian) was from Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 元末流寓湖南。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he drifted and sojourned in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Yuan he lived in Hunan as a refugee.

sentences.zh: 太祖平武昌，用為江西行省僉事，曆大理卿。

translations.literal: When the Taizu pacified Wuchang, he employed him as Jiangxi Branch Secretariat assistant commissioner and he served successively as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu took Wuchang he made him Jiangxi assistant commissioner and later minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 太祖以唐、宋皆有成律斷獄，惟元以一時行事為條格，胥吏易為奸，詔禎與李善長、劉基、陶安、滕毅等定律令。

translations.literal: The Taizu, because Tang and Song each had established statutes for adjudicating cases while the Yuan took transient actions as regulatory articles so that clerks easily committed abuses, ordered Zhen together with Li Shanchang, Liu Ji, Tao An, Teng Yi, and others to fix laws and decrees.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu noted that Tang and Song had fixed penal codes whereas the Yuan ruled by ad hoc regulations that clerks easily abused, and ordered Zhou Zhen, Li Shanchang, Liu Ji, Tao An, Teng Yi, and others to draft a code.

sentences.zh: 少卿劉惟謙、丞周湞與焉。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Liu Weiqian and Assistant Minister Zhou Zhen (Boning) also took part.
translations.idiomatic: Vice minister Liu Weiqian and assistant minister Zhou Zhen (Boning) joined them.

sentences.zh: 書成，太祖稱善。

translations.literal: When the book was finished the Taizu praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: When the code was complete Taizu praised it.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年設刑部，以禎為尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu the Ministry of Punishments was established and Zhen was made Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year one the Ministry of Punishments was set up and Zhou Zhen was made its minister.

sentences.zh: 尋改治書侍御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 明年出為廣東行省參政。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as Guangdong Branch Secretariat administrative commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Guangdong administrative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時省治初開，正官多缺，吏治鮮勸懲。

translations.literal: At that time the province's administration was newly opened and regular posts were mostly vacant, so official discipline scarcely had reward and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The province was newly established, key posts were empty, and official discipline was weak.

sentences.zh: 香山丞沖敬有治行，以勞卒官。

translations.literal: Xiangshan Assistant Magistrate Chong Jing had governing achievements and died in office from overwork.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Jing, assistant magistrate of Xiangshan, governed well and died in office from exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 禎為文祭之，聞者感動。

translations.literal: Zhen composed a text to sacrifice to him, and those who heard were moved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhen wrote a funeral elegy for him that moved all who heard it.

sentences.zh: 一時郡邑良吏雷州同知余騏孫、惠州知府萬迪、乳源知縣張安仁、清流知縣李鐸、揭陽縣丞許德、廉州知府脫因、歸善知縣木寅，禎皆列其政績以聞。

translations.literal: For a time the good officials of the prefectures and districts—Leizhou Associate Prefect Yu Qisun, Huizhou Prefect Wan Di, Ruyuan Magistrate Zhang Anren, Qingliu Magistrate Li Duo, Jieyang Assistant Magistrate Xu De, Lianzhou Prefect Tuoyin, and Guishan Magistrate Mu Yin—Zhen all listed their political achievements and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to the throne the achievements of worthy local officials of the day, including Yu Qisun of Leizhou, Wan Di of Huizhou, Zhang Anren of Ruyuan, Li Duo of Qingliu, Xu De of Jieyang, Tuoyin of Lianzhou, and Mu Yin of Guishan.

sentences.zh: 寅，土司。

translations.literal: Yin was a tribal official.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Yin was a tribal official.

sentences.zh: 脫因，蒙古人也。

translations.literal: Tuoyin was a Mongol.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoyin was Mongolian.

sentences.zh: 於是屬吏益勸。

translations.literal: Thereupon subordinate officials were the more encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate officials were thereby encouraged to do better.

sentences.zh: 三年九月召為御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year he was summoned as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year three he was recalled as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋引疾致仕。

translations.literal: Soon, citing illness, he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 帝初即位，懲元寬縱，用法太嚴，奉行者重足立。

translations.literal: When the Emperor first took the throne he punished the Yuan's lax indulgence and used the law too severely, so those who carried it out stood as if on tiptoe.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his reign the emperor reacted to Yuan laxity with harsh law enforcement that left officials terrified.

sentences.zh: 律令既具，吏士始知循守。

translations.literal: Once the laws and decrees were in place, clerks and scholars began to know how to follow and keep them.
translations.idiomatic: Once the code was in place officials finally knew the rules they had to follow.

sentences.zh: 其後數有厘正，皆以禎書為權輿雲。

translations.literal: Later there were several revisions and corrections, all taking his book as their origin, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Later revisions all traced back to his compilation, it is said.

sentences.zh: 劉惟謙，不詳何許人。

translations.literal: Liu Weiqian—his native place is not recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Weiqian's place of origin is unknown.

sentences.zh: 吳元年以才學舉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wu he was recommended for talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu year one he was recommended for scholarship.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，曆官刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In early Hongwu he served successively as Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In early Hongwu he rose to minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 六年命詳定新律，刪繁損舊，輕重得宜。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered to revise the new code in detail, cutting redundancy and reducing old provisions so that severity and leniency were fitting.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he was ordered to refine the new code, trimming excess and old provisions until penalties fit the crimes.

sentences.zh: 帝親加裁定頒行焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally added revisions and corrections and promulgated it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally revised it and promulgated the result.

sentences.zh: 後坐事免。

translations.literal: Later, implicated in an affair, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was later dismissed after being implicated in a case.

sentences.zh: 周湞，字伯甯，鄱陽人。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhen, style name Boning, was a native of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhen (Boning) was from Poyang.

sentences.zh: 江西十才子之一也，官亦至刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was one of the Ten Talents of Jiangxi, and his office also reached Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: One of Jiangxi's Ten Talents, he too rose to minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 終洪武世，為刑部者亦幾四十人，楊靖最著，而端復初、李質、黎光、劉敏亦有名。

translations.literal: Through the entire Hongwu reign those who served as Minister of Punishments numbered nearly forty; Yang Jing was the most renowned, while Duan Fuchu, Li Zhi, Li Guang, and Liu Min also had fame.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly forty men held the ministry of punishments during Hongwu; Yang Jing was the most famous, but Duan Fuchu, Li Zhi, Li Guang, and Liu Min were also well known.

sentences.zh: 復初，字以善，溧水人。

translations.literal: Fuchu, style name Yishan, was a native of Lishui.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Fuchu (Yishan) was from Lishui.

sentences.zh: 子貢裔也，從省文，稱端氏。

translations.literal: A descendant of Zigong's line, he followed the abbreviated form in writing and was called the Duan clan.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant of Confucius' disciple Zigong, he used the abbreviated clan name Duan in documents.

sentences.zh: 元末為小吏。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he was a petty clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan he served as a petty clerk.

sentences.zh: 常遇春鎮金華，召致幕下。

translations.literal: When Chang Yuchun garrisoned Jinhua he summoned and brought him to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun summoned him to his staff when garrisoning Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 未幾，辭去。

translations.literal: Before long he resigned and left.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left the post.

sentences.zh: 太祖知其名，召為徽州府經歷。

translations.literal: The Taizu knew his name and summoned him as registrar of Huizhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu knew his reputation and made him registrar of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 令民自實田，ＢＺ為圖籍，積弊盡刷。

translations.literal: He ordered the people to report their own fields themselves, compiled registers into maps and records, and long-standing abuses were entirely swept away.
translations.idiomatic: He had households declare their own land, compiled the data into registers and cadasters, and cleared away entrenched abuses.

sentences.zh: 稍遷至磨勘司令。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to verification-and-audit command.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to head the verification-and-audit office.

sentences.zh: 時官署新立，案牘填委，復初鉤稽無遺。

translations.literal: At that time government offices were newly established and case documents piled up; Fuchu audited without omission.
translations.idiomatic: With new agencies drowning in paperwork, Fuchu audited accounts with nothing overlooked.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗廷譽之。

translations.literal: The Emperor once praised him in court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once praised him at court.

sentences.zh: 性嚴峭，人不敢幹以私。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and precipitous; men did not dare to importune him with private matters.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and unyielding, he would brook no private favor.

sentences.zh: 僚屬多貪敗，復初獨以清白免。

translations.literal: Many colleagues were greedy and ruined, but Fuchu alone escaped through integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Many colleagues fell to corruption while he alone kept his integrity.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年，超拜刑部尚書，用法平。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu he was exceptionally promoted to Minister of Punishments and applied the law evenly.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year four he was promoted out of turn to minister of punishments and applied the law fairly.

sentences.zh: 杭州飛糧事覺，逮系百餘人。

translations.literal: The Hangzhou flying-grain affair came to light and more than a hundred persons were arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: A grain-surplus fraud case in Hangzhou came to light and over a hundred people were arrested.

sentences.zh: 詔復初往治，誠偽立辨，知府以下皆服罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Fuchu to go and try it; truth and falsehood were immediately distinguished, and from the prefect down all acknowledged guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Fuchu to investigate; he quickly distinguished truth from fraud, and the prefect and his subordinates all confessed.

sentences.zh: 明年出為湖廣參政。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as Huguang administrative commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Huguang administrative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 令民來歸者，復其賦一年。

translations.literal: He ordered that those among the people who came back to submit would have their tax remitted for one year.
translations.idiomatic: He exempted returning refugees from taxes for one year.

sentences.zh: 流亡畢集。

translations.literal: The exiled and displaced all gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Exiles and refugees all returned.

sentences.zh: 以治辦聞。

translations.literal: He was known for effective administration.
translations.idiomatic: He became known for effective governance.

sentences.zh: 坐事召還，卒。

translations.literal: Implicated in an affair he was summoned back and died.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled after being implicated in a case, he died on the way.

sentences.zh: 子孝文，翰林待詔；

translations.literal: His son Xiaowen was a Hanlin attendant;
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaowen became a Hanlin attendant;

sentences.zh: 孝思，翰林侍書。

translations.literal: Xiaosi was a Hanlin attendant-calligrapher.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosi served as a Hanlin attendant-calligrapher.

sentences.zh: 先後使朝鮮，並著清節，朝鮮人為立「雙清館」雲。

translations.literal: They were sent as envoys to Korea in succession and both showed pure integrity; the Koreans erected for them the "Twin Clarity Hall," it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Both served as envoys to Korea and won renown for integrity; Koreans built the "Twin Clarity Hall" in their honor, it is said.

sentences.zh: 李質，字文彬，德慶人。

translations.literal: Li Zhi, style name Wenbin, was a native of Deqing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi (Wenbin) was from Deqing.

sentences.zh: 有材略。

translations.literal: He had talent and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He was talented and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 元末居何真麾下，嘗募兵平德慶亂民，旁郡多賴其保障。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he dwelt under He Zhen's command, once raised troops to pacify rebellious people in Deqing, and neighboring prefectures largely relied on his protection.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yuan he served under He Zhen, raised troops to quell unrest in Deqing, and neighboring districts relied on his protection.

sentences.zh: 名士客嶺南者，茶陵劉三吾、江右伯顏子中、羊城孫蕡、建安張智等，皆禮之。

translations.literal: Famous scholars who sojourned in Lingnan—Chaling's Liu Sanwu, Jiangyou's Bayan Zizhong, Yangcheng's Sun Zan, Jian'an's Zhang Zhi, and others—he all treated with ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He honored famous scholars who came to the south, including Liu Sanwu of Chaling, Bayan Zizhong from Jiangxi, Sun Zan of Guangzhou, and Zhang Zhi of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，從真降，授中書斷事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu he followed Zhen in surrendering and was appointed an adjudicator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year one he submitted with He Zhen and was made a Secretariat adjudicator.

sentences.zh: 明年改都督府斷事，強力執法。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to an adjudicator in the Chief Military Commission and enforced the law with force.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became a military commission adjudicator and enforced the law firmly.

sentences.zh: 五年擢刑部侍郎，進尚書，治獄平恕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments, advanced to Minister, and tried cases with even leniency.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he rose to vice then minister of punishments and judged cases with measured leniency.

sentences.zh: 遣振饑山東，禦制詩餞之。

translations.literal: He was sent to relieve famine in Shandong and the Emperor composed a poem to feast him on departure.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to relieve famine in Shandong, he was farewelled with an imperial poem.

sentences.zh: 尋出為浙江行省參政。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Zhejiang Branch Secretariat administrative commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted as Zhejiang administrative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 居三年，惠績著聞。

translations.literal: After three years in office his benevolent achievements were renowned.
translations.idiomatic: After three years his benevolent rule was widely praised.

sentences.zh: 帝念質老，召還。

translations.literal: The Emperor, mindful that Zhi was old, summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of his age, the emperor recalled him.

sentences.zh: 嘗入見便殿，訪時政。

translations.literal: He once entered to be received in the informal hall and was asked about current policy.
translations.idiomatic: He was once received in the informal hall and questioned on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 質直言無隱。

translations.literal: Zhi spoke straight without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi spoke frankly and held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 拜靖江王右相。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Chancellor of the Prince of Jingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made right chancellor to the Prince of Jingjiang.

sentences.zh: 王罪廢，質竟坐死。

translations.literal: When the prince's crime led to his abolition, Zhi in the end was implicated and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was disgraced and stripped of his title, Li Zhi was executed as an accomplice.

sentences.zh: 黎光，東莞人。

translations.literal: Li Guang was a native of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang was from Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 以鄉薦拜御史，巡蘇州，請振水災，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Recommended through the village presentation, he was appointed censor, toured Suzhou, requested relief for flood victims, and fully preserved very many lives.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended locally, he became a censor, toured Suzhou, secured flood relief, and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 巡鳳陽，上封事悉切時弊，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: Touring Fengyang, he submitted a sealed memorial entirely cutting to the abuses of the time, and the Emperor commended it.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting Fengyang, he sent a sealed memorial on timely abuses that the emperor praised.

sentences.zh: 洪武九年，擢刑部侍郎，執法不阿，為御史大夫陳甯所忌，坐事死貶所。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongwu he was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments; he enforced the law without bending, was resented by Censor-in-Chief Chen Ning, implicated in an affair, and died at the place of demotion.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year nine he became vice minister of punishments; his impartial enforcement earned the hatred of Censor-in-Chief Chen Ning, and after being implicated in a case he died in exile.

sentences.zh: 劉敏，肅寧人。

translations.literal: Liu Min was a native of Suining.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Min was from Suining.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，為中書省吏。

translations.literal: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he became a clerk in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for filial piety and integrity, he became a Secretariat clerk.

sentences.zh: 嘗暮市蘆龍江，旦載於家，俾妻織蓆，鬻以奉母。

translations.literal: He would at dusk buy reeds on the Lulong River, at dawn carry them home, have his wife weave mats, and sell them to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Each evening he bought reeds on the Lulong River, brought them home at dawn for his wife to weave into mats he sold to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 而後，入治事。

translations.literal: Only afterward would he enter to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Only then would he go to the office.

sentences.zh: 性廉介，或遺之瓷瓦器，亦不受。

translations.literal: His nature was incorrupt and aloof; even if someone gave him porcelain or tile vessels he would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Incorruptible and reserved, he would not accept even a gift of porcelain or tiles.

sentences.zh: 為楚相府錄事，中書以沒官女婦給文臣家，眾勸其請給以事母。

translations.literal: Serving as recorder of the Chu prince's establishment, the Secretariat because of confiscated palace women marrying them off to civil officials' households—the crowd urged him to request an allotment to serve his mother.
translations.idiomatic: As recorder for the Chu princely establishment, when the Secretariat distributed confiscated palace women to officials' households, colleagues urged him to request one to help care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 敏固辭曰：「事母，子婦事，何預他人。

translations.literal: Min firmly declined, saying: "Serving one's mother is a daughter-in-law's affair—what has that to do with others?
translations.idiomatic: Min firmly refused, saying, "Caring for one's mother is a daughter-in-law's duty—what business is that of anyone else?

sentences.zh: 」及省臣敗，吏多坐誅，敏獨無所預。

translations.literal: "When the provincial ministers fell, many clerks were executed for involvement, but Min alone had no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: "When the provincial ministers were purged, many clerks were executed for complicity, but Min alone was untouched.

sentences.zh: 帝賢之，擢工部侍郎，改刑部。

translations.literal: The Emperor regarded him as worthy and promoted him to Vice Minister of Works, then changed him to Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired him, made him vice minister of works, then transferred him to punishments.

sentences.zh: 出為徽州府同知，有惠政，卒於官。

translations.literal: He went out as Tongzhi of Huizhou Prefecture, had benevolent administration, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as Huizhou associate prefect, he governed benevolently and died in office.

sentences.zh: 楊靖，字仲甯，山陽人。

translations.literal: Yang Jing, style name Zhongning, was a native of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jing (Zhongning) was from Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 洪武十八年進士，選吏科庶起士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the eighteenth year of Hongwu, he was selected as a Hanlin probationer in the Ministry of Personnel section.
translations.idiomatic: A Hongwu year-eighteen jinshi, he was chosen as a Hanlin probationer in the Ministry of Personnel track.

sentences.zh: 明年擢戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 時任諸司者，率進士及太學生，然時有不法者。

translations.literal: At that time those appointed in the various departments were mostly jinshi and Imperial University students, yet from time to time there were men who did not keep the law.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in the ministries were then mostly jinshi and imperial university graduates, yet some still broke the law.

sentences.zh: 帝制《大誥》，舉通政使蔡瑄、左通政茹瑺、工部侍郎秦逵及靖以諷厲之曰：「此亦進士太學生也，能率職以稱朕心。

translations.literal: The Emperor composed the Great Admonitions, citing Commissioner of Transmission Cai Xuan, Left Commissioner Ru Chao, Vice Minister of Works Qin Kui, and Jing to admonish and encourage them, saying: "These too are jinshi and Imperial University students, able to lead their duties to suit my heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote the Great Admonitions and held up Cai Xuan, commissioner of transmission, Ru Chao, left commissioner, Qin Kui, vice minister of works, and Jing as examples, exhorting others: "These men too were jinshi and imperial university graduates, yet they perform their duties in a way that satisfies me.

sentences.zh: 」其見稱如此。

translations.literal: " Thus was he praised.
translations.idiomatic: That was how highly he was regarded.

sentences.zh: 二十二年進尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 明年五月詔在京官三年皆遷調，著為令。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the next year an edict declared that capital officials after three years all transfer posts, established as statute.
translations.idiomatic: The following May the court ordered that every capital official be rotated after three years, and made it permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 乃以刑部尚書趙勉與靖換官。

translations.literal: Thereupon Minister of Punishments Zhao Min and Jing were made to exchange offices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Min, minister of punishments, and Jing then swapped posts.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「愚民犯法，如啖飲食。

translations.literal: He instructed them, saying: "When foolish commoners violate the law, it is like eating and drinking.
translations.idiomatic: He told them: "Ignorant people break the law as readily as they eat and drink.

sentences.zh: 設法防之，犯者益眾。

translations.literal: Setting up laws to guard against it, offenders instead grow more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The more laws you devise to stop them, the more offenders you get.

sentences.zh: 推恕行仁，或能感化。

translations.literal: Pushing forgiveness and practicing benevolence, perhaps one can transform them.
translations.idiomatic: Forbearance and humane governance may actually reform them.

sentences.zh: 自今惟犯十惡並殺人者死，餘罪皆令輸粟北邊。

translations.literal: From now on only those who commit the Ten Abominations together with murderers die; all remaining crimes are ordered to pay grain to the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth only the ten abominations and murder carry the death penalty; all other crimes will be commuted to delivering grain to the northern border.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「在京獄囚，卿等覆奏，朕親審決，猶恐有失。

translations.literal: " He also said: "For prisoners in the capital jails, you review and memorialize, and I personally examine and decide — yet I still fear mistakes.
translations.idiomatic: " He added: "Capital prisoners come before you for review and then to me for final judgment, and I still worry about error.

sentences.zh: 在外各官所擬，豈能盡當？

translations.literal: The sentences proposed by each official in the provinces — how can they all be correct?
translations.idiomatic: How can provincial officials' recommendations always be right?

sentences.zh: 卿等當詳讞，然後遣官審決。

translations.literal: You should deliberate the cases in detail, then dispatch officials to examine and decide.
translations.idiomatic: You must examine each case thoroughly before sending officers to confirm the verdict.

sentences.zh: 」靖承旨研辨，多所平反。

translations.literal: " Jing received the order and studied and distinguished cases, reversing many wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: Jing followed the edict, scrutinized cases, and overturned many verdicts.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his work.

sentences.zh: 嘗鞫一武弁，門卒撿其身，得大珠，屬僚驚異。

translations.literal: Once when trying a military officer, a gate guard searched his person and found a large pearl; subordinate officials were startled and wondered.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while questioning a military officer, a gate guard frisked him and found a huge pearl, to the amazement of Jing's staff.

sentences.zh: 靖徐曰：「偽也，安有珠大如此者乎。

translations.literal: Jing said slowly: "It is a fake — how could there be a pearl this large?
translations.idiomatic: Jing said calmly, "It is counterfeit. How could a pearl be this big?

sentences.zh: 」碎之。

translations.literal: " He smashed it.
translations.idiomatic: He smashed it.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，歎曰：「靖此舉，有四善焉。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he sighed and said: "In this act Jing has four virtues.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, the emperor sighed and said, "Jing's conduct shows four kinds of excellence.

sentences.zh: 不獻朕求悅，一善也；

translations.literal: Not presenting it to me to win favor — the first virtue;
translations.idiomatic: He did not bring it to me to curry favor — first.

sentences.zh: 不窮追投獻，二善也；

translations.literal: Not pursuing thoroughly who had presented it — the second virtue;
translations.idiomatic: He did not launch a hunt for whoever had tried to bribe him — second.

sentences.zh: 不獎門卒，杜小人僥倖，三善也；

translations.literal: Not rewarding the gate guard, blocking petty men's lucky chances — the third virtue;
translations.idiomatic: He did not reward the guard, thereby shutting off opportunism among small men — third.

sentences.zh: 千金之珠卒然而至，略不動心，有過人之智，應變之才，四善也。」

translations.literal: A pearl worth a thousand gold arriving suddenly, yet he was scarcely moved — having wisdom surpassing others and talent for meeting change — the fourth virtue."
translations.idiomatic: A pearl worth a fortune turned up in an instant, yet he was barely stirred — showing exceptional judgment and presence of mind. That is the fourth excellence."

sentences.zh: 二十六年，兼太子賓客，並給二祿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he additionally served as Guest of the Heir Apparent, and both salaries were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 he also became guest of the heir apparent and drew two stipends.

sentences.zh: 已，坐事免。

translations.literal: Before long, because of an affair he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was removed from office for an offense.

sentences.zh: 會征龍州趙宗壽，詔靖諭安南輸粟餉師。

translations.literal: At the time of the campaign against Zhao Zongshou of Longzhou, Jing was ordered to instruct Annan to deliver grain to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched against Zhao Zongshou of Longzhou, Jing was sent to demand grain tribute from Annan.

sentences.zh: 以白衣往。

translations.literal: He went in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled as a commoner, without office.

sentences.zh: 安南相黎一元以陸運險艱，欲不奉詔。

translations.literal: Annan's chancellor Li Yiyuan, because overland transport was dangerous and arduous, wished not to obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Annan chancellor Li Yiyuan, citing the hazards of overland transport, tried to refuse.

sentences.zh: 靖宣示反覆開諭，且許以水運。

translations.literal: Jing proclaimed the edict repeatedly and enlightened them, and moreover promised water transport.
translations.idiomatic: Jing read the decree again and again, argued patiently, and offered shipment by water.

sentences.zh: 一元乃輸粟二萬，至沲海江別造浮橋以達龍州。

translations.literal: Yiyuan then delivered twenty thousand piculs of grain; at the Tuohai River he separately built a floating bridge to reach Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yiyuan finally sent twenty thousand piculs, and at the Tuohai River built a pontoon bridge to reach Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，拜靖左都御史。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and appointed Jing Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and made Jing left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 靖公忠有智略，善理繁劇，治獄明察而不事深文。

translations.literal: Jing was fair, loyal, and possessed strategy; he was skilled at managing complexity, and in judging cases was perceptive yet did not pursue harsh statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, loyal, and resourceful, he handled heavy workloads well and tried cases shrewdly without pedantic legalism.

sentences.zh: 寵遇最厚，同列無與比。

translations.literal: Imperial favor was thickest for him; none among his peers could compare.
translations.idiomatic: No colleague enjoyed greater favor.

sentences.zh: 三十年七月，坐為鄉人代改訴冤狀草，為御史所劾。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the thirtieth year, because he had revised a draft petition of grievance on behalf of a fellow townsman, he was impeached by a censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 30 he was impeached for editing a neighbor's complaint of injustice.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，遂賜死。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and thereupon granted him death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered him to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 時年三十八。

translations.literal: At the time he was thirty-eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 時有淩漢，字鬥南，原武人。

translations.literal: At the time there was Ling Han, style name Dounan, a native of Yuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Around the same time there was Ling Han (Dounan), from Yuanwu.

sentences.zh: 以秀才舉，獻《烏鵲論》。

translations.literal: Recommended as a xiucai, he presented "On Crows and Magpies."
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a xiucai by submitting his "Discourse on Crows and Magpies."

sentences.zh: 授官，歷任御史。

translations.literal: He received office and successively served as censor.
translations.idiomatic: He received an appointment and rose through censorial posts.

sentences.zh: 巡按陝西，疏所部疾困數事。

translations.literal: Touring and inspecting Shaanxi, he memorialized several matters of distress in his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On circuit in Shaanxi he reported several hardships afflicting the province.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，召其子賜衣鈔。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved, and summoned his son to bestow robes and paper money.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and rewarded his son with robes and cash.

sentences.zh: 漢鞫獄平允。

translations.literal: Han judged cases impartially.
translations.idiomatic: Han heard cases with evenhanded justice.

sentences.zh: 及還京，有德漢者，邀置酒，欲厚贈以金。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital, one who admired Han's virtue invited him to wine and wished to give him gold generously.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, an admirer treated him to wine and tried to press a hefty gift of gold on him.

sentences.zh: 漢曰：「酒可飲，金不可受也。

translations.literal: Han said: "Wine may be drunk; gold may not be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Han replied, "I will drink your wine, but I cannot take your gold.

sentences.zh: 」帝聞之嘉歎，擢右都御史。

translations.literal: " When the Emperor heard, he praised and sighed, and promoted him to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor heard and commended him, then promoted him to right censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時詹徽為左，論議不合，每面折徽，徽銜之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhan Hui was on the left; their discussions did not agree, and he every time rebutted Hui to his face; Hui bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Hui held the left post; the two clashed in council, Han regularly humiliating him in debate, and Hui nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 左遷刑部侍郎，改禮部。

translations.literal: He was transferred down to Vice Minister of Punishments, then changed to Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Han was demoted to vice minister of punishments, then shifted to rites.

sentences.zh: 後為徽所劾，降左僉都御史。

translations.literal: Later he was impeached by Hui and demoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Hui later had him impeached and reduced him to left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 帝憫其衰，令歸田裏。

translations.literal: The Emperor pitied his age and ordered him to return to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, pitying his years, let him retire to his hometown.

sentences.zh: 漢以徽在，有後憂，不敢去。

translations.literal: Han, because Hui remained, had worry for what might come later, and did not dare leave.
translations.idiomatic: With Hui still in power, Han feared later reprisals and stayed on.

sentences.zh: 歲餘徽誅，復擢右僉都御史。

translations.literal: After more than a year Hui was executed, and he was again promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Hui was executed, and Han was restored as right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋致仕歸。

translations.literal: Before long he resigned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired for good.

sentences.zh: 漢出言不檢，居官屢躓。

translations.literal: Han's speech was unguarded; in office he stumbled repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: His tongue got him into trouble again and again.

sentences.zh: 然以廉直見知於帝，故終得保全。

translations.literal: Yet because of integrity and uprightness he was known to the Emperor, and so in the end he was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued his probity, however, and he survived with his life intact.

sentences.zh: 又吳人嚴德瑉，由御史擢左僉都御史，以疾求歸。

translations.literal: Also Yan Demin of Wu, from censor was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief; because of illness he requested leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: Another case was Yan Demin of Wu, promoted from censor to left vice censor-in-chief, who asked to go home on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，黥其面，謫戍南丹。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry, tattooed his face, and banished him to garrison Nan Dan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, branded his face, and exiled him to Nan Dan.

sentences.zh: 遇赦放還。

translations.literal: He met an amnesty and was released to return.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty eventually brought him home.

sentences.zh: 布衣徒步，自齒齊民。

translations.literal: In plain robes he went on foot, counting himself among ordinary people.
translations.idiomatic: He dressed as a commoner and walked everywhere like any other townsman.

sentences.zh: 宣德中猶存。

translations.literal: In the Xuande reign he was still alive.
translations.idiomatic: He was still living in the Xuande era.

sentences.zh: 嘗以事為御史所逮，德瑉跪堂下，自言曾在台勾當公事，曉三尺法。

translations.literal: Once when something led a censor to seize him, Demin knelt below the hall and said himself that he had formerly handled public business at the censorate and knew the three-foot law.
translations.idiomatic: Once when a censor detained him over some matter, Demin knelt in the hall and said he had once served in the censorate and knew the code.

sentences.zh: 御史問何官。

translations.literal: The censor asked what office he had held.
translations.idiomatic: The censor asked what rank he had held.

sentences.zh: 答言：「洪武中台長，所謂嚴德瑉是也。

translations.literal: He answered: "In Hongwu I was chief of the desk — the one called Yan Demin is I.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Under Hongwu I was head of the censorate — Yan Demin, that is me.

sentences.zh: 」御史大驚，揖起之。

translations.literal: " The censor was greatly startled and bowed to raise him.
translations.idiomatic: " The censor was shocked and helped him up with a bow.

sentences.zh: 次日往謁，則擔囊徙矣。

translations.literal: The next day he went to visit, but Demin had shouldered his bag and moved away.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the censor called, only to find Demin had packed up and left.

sentences.zh: 有教授與飲，見其面黥，戴敝冠，問：「老人犯何法？

translations.literal: A district instructor drinking with him saw his tattooed face and worn cap and asked: "Old sir, what law did you violate?
translations.idiomatic: A local instructor shared wine with him, noticed the facial brand and shabby hat, and asked, "Elder, what crime did you commit?

sentences.zh: 」瑉述前事，因言「先時國法甚嚴，仕者不保首領，此敝冠不易戴也。

translations.literal: " Demin recounted the former affair, and then said: "Formerly state law was very strict; those who served could not keep their heads — this worn cap is not easily worn.
translations.idiomatic: " Demin told the story and added, "In those days the law was merciless — officials could not expect to keep their heads. This shabby cap is not lightly worn.

sentences.zh: 」乃北面拱手，稱「聖恩，聖恩」雲。

translations.literal: " Thereupon facing north he cupped his hands and said "sage grace, sage grace," and so on.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he turned north, bowed with clasped hands, and murmured, "The sage's mercy, the sage's mercy."

sentences.zh: 單安仁，字德夫，濠人。

translations.literal: Dan Anren, style name Defu, was a man of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Dan Anren (Defu) was from Hao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少為府吏。

translations.literal: In youth he was a prefectural clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerk in the prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 元末江淮兵亂，安仁集義兵保鄉里，授樞密判官。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuan the Yangtze-Huai region had military turmoil; Anren gathered righteous troops to protect the homeland and was appointed Pacification Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When war convulsed the Jianghuai region late in Yuan, he raised a militia to defend his home and was made vice commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 從鎮南王孛羅普化守揚州。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince Zhennan Boluohuata in guarding Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Prince Zhennan Boluohuata defending Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時群雄四起，安仁歎曰：「此輩皆為人驅除耳。

translations.literal: When at the time numerous strongmen rose everywhere, Anren sighed and said: "These men are all being used to drive others away.
translations.idiomatic: As warlords sprang up on every side, Anren sighed and said, "These fellows are only clearing the way for someone else.

sentences.zh: 王者之興，當自有別。

translations.literal: When a true king rises, there should be something separate.
translations.idiomatic: The man destined to rule will come from elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 」鎮南王為長槍軍所逐，安仁無所屬，聞太祖定集慶，乃曰：「此誠是已。

translations.literal: " The Prince Zhennan was driven out by the Long Spear Army; Anren had nowhere he belonged; hearing that the Taizu had pacified Jiqing, he then said: "This truly is he.
translations.idiomatic: " When Long Spear troops expelled Prince Zhennan, Anren was left masterless; hearing that the Taizu had secured Jiqing (Nanjing), he said, "This is the one.

sentences.zh: 」率眾歸附。

translations.literal: " He led the masses to submit and attach.
translations.idiomatic: " He led his followers to surrender.

sentences.zh: 太祖悅，即命將其軍守鎮江。

translations.literal: The Taizu was pleased and at once ordered him to lead his army to guard Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu welcomed him and immediately put his troops under him to defend Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 嚴飭軍伍，敵不敢犯。

translations.literal: He rigorously drilled the army; enemies did not dare invade.
translations.idiomatic: He disciplined his troops so tightly that no enemy dared approach.

sentences.zh: 移守常州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to guard Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then posted to Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 其子叛，降張士誠，太祖知安仁忠謹，弗疑也。

translations.literal: His son rebelled and surrendered to Zhang Shicheng; the Taizu knew Anren was loyal and careful, and did not doubt him.
translations.idiomatic: His son defected to Zhang Shicheng, but the Taizu, trusting Anren's loyalty, did not suspect him.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷浙江副使。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to be Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he became Zhejiang vice surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 悍帥橫斂民，名曰「寨糧」，安仁置於法。

translations.literal: Fierce commanders forcibly collected from the people what was called "stockade grain"; Anren placed them under the law.
translations.idiomatic: Bullying generals extorted "stockade grain" from peasants; Anren prosecuted them.

sentences.zh: 進按察使，征為中書左司郎中，佐李善長裁斷。

translations.literal: He was promoted Surveillance Commissioner, summoned as Left Section Director in the Central Secretariat, and assisted Li Shanchang in adjudication.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to surveillance commissioner, he was called to the Secretariat as a director and helped Li Shanchang pass judgment.

sentences.zh: 調瑞州守禦千戶，入為將作卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to defensive commandant of Ruizhou Guard, then entered as Director of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Ruizhou defensive commandant, then became director of the Directorate of Works.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年擢工部尚書，仍領將作事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu he was promoted Minister of Works, still overseeing Directorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 1 he was made minister of works while continuing to run the directorate.

sentences.zh: 安仁精敏多智計，諸所營造，大小中程，甚稱帝意。

translations.literal: Anren was keen and had many stratagems; in every construction large and small he met the standard, greatly suiting the Emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and full of expedients, he brought every project in on schedule and won the emperor's praise.

sentences.zh: 逾年改兵部尚書。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was changed to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he moved to the war ministry.

sentences.zh: 請老歸，賜田三千畝，牛七十角，歲給尚書半俸。

translations.literal: He requested to retire and return home; he was granted three thousand mu of fields, seventy head of cattle, and half a Minister's salary yearly.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire and received three thousand mu of land, seventy cattle, and half pay for life.

sentences.zh: 六年起山東參政。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was recalled as Shandong Administrative Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was recalled to serve as Shandong vice administrator.

sentences.zh: 懇辭，許之。

translations.literal: He earnestly declined; this was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded age and was excused.

sentences.zh: 家居，嘗奏請浚儀真南壩至樸樹灣，以便官民輸挽；

translations.literal: Dwelling at home, he once memorialized requesting dredging from the south dam at Yizhen to Pushu Bay, to facilitate transport for officials and people;
translations.idiomatic: At home he proposed dredging from Yizhen's southern levee to Pushu Bay to ease hauling for officials and commoners;

sentences.zh: 疏轉運河江都深港以防淤淺；

translations.literal: dredging the Grand Canal's deep harbor at Jiangdu to prevent silting shallow;
translations.idiomatic: clearing Jiangdu's deep harbor on the Grand Canal to stop silting;

sentences.zh: 移瓜州倉ＣＣ置揚子橋西，免大江風潮之患。

translations.literal: moving the Guazhou granary to west of Yangzi Bridge, eliminating the calamity of great-river wind and waves.
translations.idiomatic: and relocating the Guazhou granary west of Yangzi Bridge to spare grain from the Yangtze's storms.

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，再授兵部尚書，致仕。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words and again appointed him Minister of War, then retired from service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the advice, reappointed him minister of war, and let him retire again.

sentences.zh: 初，尚書階正三品。

translations.literal: At first the ministerial rank was Regular Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers had initially been third rank.

sentences.zh: 十三年，中書省罷，始進為正二。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Central Secretariat was abolished; only then was it advanced to Regular Second Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the Secretariat was abolished in year 13 the rank rose to second.

sentences.zh: 而安仁致仕在前。

translations.literal: Yet Anren had retired from service before this.
translations.idiomatic: Anren had already retired by then.

sentences.zh: 帝念安仁勳舊，二十年特授資善大夫。

translations.literal: The Emperor remembering Anren's achievements as founding companion, in the twentieth year specially appointed him Honorary Grand Master of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of his founding service, the emperor in year 20 granted him the honorary title Grand Master of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: In that year in the twelfth month he died, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died that December at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 徐州硃守仁者，字元夫。

translations.literal: Zhu Shouren of Xuzhou, style name Yuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shouren of Xuzhou (Yuanfu).

sentences.zh: 元末亦以保障功官樞密同知，守舒城。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuan he likewise because of guarding-and-protection achievement was made Tongzhi of the Secretariat of Military Affairs and guarded Shucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Like Anren, he won a pacification post late in Yuan as tongzhi in the military secretariat and held Shucheng.

sentences.zh: 明兵下廬州，以城來歸。

translations.literal: When Ming troops descended on Luzhou, he brought the city to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming forces took Luzhou he surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 曆官工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He passed through offices as Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年進尚書，奉命察山東官吏，稱旨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu he was advanced to Minister, ordered to inspect Shandong officials, and met the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 4 he was made minister and sent to inspect Shandong officials; his report pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 尋改北平行省參政，以饋餉不繼，謫蒼梧知縣。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Administrative Vice Commissioner of the Beiping Branch Secretariat; because provisions and supplies did not continue, he was demoted to magistrate of Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted as Beiping vice administrator, but when supply lines failed he was demoted to magistrate of Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 初，守仁知袁州，撫安創殘，民甚德之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shouren governed Yuanzhou, he soothed and settled the wounded remnant; the people greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as prefect of Yuanzhou, he had nursed a war-torn region back to order, and the people loved him for it.

sentences.zh: 至是連知容州、高唐州，皆有善政。

translations.literal: At this time he governed in succession Rongzhou and Gaotangzhou, and in each had good administration.
translations.idiomatic: Now, serving in turn at Rongzhou and Gaotang, he governed well in both posts.

sentences.zh: 十年進四川布政使，治尚簡嚴。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was advanced to Sichuan Pacification Commissioner; his governance valued simplicity and severity.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he became Sichuan pacification commissioner, ruling with spare severity.

sentences.zh: 以年老致仕。

translations.literal: Because of old age he retired from service.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on grounds of age.

sentences.zh: 坐事罰輸作，特宥之。

translations.literal: Implicated in an affair he was punished to labor at transport works; he was specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted in a case, he was sentenced to corvée labor but received a special pardon.

sentences.zh: 十五年，雲南平，改威楚、開南等路宣撫司為楚雄府，遂命守仁知府事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Yunnan was pacified; the Weichu, Kainan, and other circuit Pacification Commissions were changed to Chuxiong Prefecture, and Shouren was then ordered to administer the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15, after Yunnan was pacified, the Weichu and Kainan pacification offices became Chuxiong Prefecture, and Shouren was named prefect.

sentences.zh: 招集流移，均徭役，建學校，境內大治。

translations.literal: He gathered and collected the displaced, equalized corvée and levies, built schools, and within the borders there was great order.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled refugees, balanced labor levies, founded schools, and brought the prefecture to good order.

sentences.zh: 二十八年上計入朝，郡人垂涕送之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he presented accounts and entered court; the people of the commandery wept as they sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to court in year 28 for the annual review, the people of his commandery saw him off in tears.

sentences.zh: 拜太僕卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Master of Studs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand master of studs.

sentences.zh: 首請立牧馬草場于江北滁州諸處。

translations.literal: He was the first to request establishing horse-pasture meadows north of the Yangtze at Chuzhou and other places.
translations.idiomatic: He was first to propose horse pastures north of the Yangtze around Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 所轄十四監九十八群。

translations.literal: Under his jurisdiction were fourteen studs and ninety-eight herds.
translations.idiomatic: His office oversaw fourteen studs and ninety-eight herds.

sentences.zh: 馬大蕃息。

translations.literal: Horses greatly multiplied and thrived.
translations.idiomatic: The herds multiplied greatly.

sentences.zh: 馬政之修，自守仁始。

translations.literal: The restoration of horse administration began with Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: The revival of Ming horse policy began with Shouren.

sentences.zh: 久之，致仕。

translations.literal: After a long time he retired from service.
translations.idiomatic: In time he retired again.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，入朝，遇疾卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle he entered court, encountered illness, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongle reign he came to court, fell ill on the journey, and died.

sentences.zh: 八年授工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 時造鳳陽宮殿。

translations.literal: At the time the Fengyang palace halls were being built.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then building the palaces at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 帝坐殿中，若有人持兵鬥殿脊者。

translations.literal: The Emperor sat in the hall as if someone were holding weapons and fighting on the hall ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, seated in the hall, seemed to see armed figures fighting on the roof ridge.

sentences.zh: 太師李善長奏諸工匠用厭鎮法，帝將盡殺之。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Li Shanchang memorialized that the craftsmen had used sorcery to suppress and bind; the Emperor was about to kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Li Shanchang reported that the craftsmen had used malign sorcery, and the emperor prepared to execute them all.

sentences.zh: 祥為分別交替不在工者，並鐵石匠皆不預，活者千數。

translations.literal: Xiang for them distinguished those on rotation not presently at the works, and ironworkers and stoneworkers alike were not included; those who lived numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang sorted out artisans on rotation who were not on site, and excluded iron- and stoneworkers as well, saving thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 營謹身殿，有司列中匠為上匠，帝怒其罔，命棄市。

translations.literal: When building the Hall of Self-Discipline, the responsible officials listed middle artisans as top artisans; the Emperor was angry at their deception and ordered execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: While the Hall of Self-Discipline was under construction, officials mislabeled journeymen as master craftsmen; the emperor, furious at the fraud, ordered them executed.

sentences.zh: 祥在側，爭曰：「奏對不實，竟殺人，恐非法。

translations.literal: Xiang was at his side and argued: "The memorial reply was untrue; to kill people outright, I fear, is not lawful.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang stood beside him and protested, "The report was false — to execute them anyway would be unlawful.

sentences.zh: 」得旨用腐刑。

translations.literal: " He received an order to use castration punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered castration instead.

sentences.zh: 祥復徐奏曰：「腐，廢人矣，莫若杖而使工。

translations.literal: Xiang again slowly memorialized: "Castration makes a man useless; better to flog him and let him work.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang pressed on gently: "Castration ruins a man for life — better to beat him and keep him on the job.

sentences.zh: 」帝可之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 明年改天下行省為承宣佈政司。

translations.literal: The next year all-under-Heaven branch secretariats were changed to Pacification and Redistribution Branch Secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the empire's branch secretariats were reorganized as pacification commissions.

sentences.zh: 以北平重地，特授祥，三年治行稱第一。

translations.literal: Because Beiping was a weighty region, Xiang was specially appointed; in three years his governance was called first.
