translations.idiomatic: Beiping being strategically vital, Xiang was specially posted there, and within three years his record ranked first.

sentences.zh: 為胡惟庸所惡，坐營建擾民，謫知嘉興府。

translations.literal: He was hated by Hu Weiyong; implicated for construction disturbing the people, he was demoted to prefect of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Weiyong turned against him; charged with harassing the people through building projects, he was demoted to prefect of Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 惟庸誅，復召為工部尚書。

translations.literal: When Weiyong was executed, he was again summoned as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After Hu Weiyong's execution he was recalled as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「讒臣害汝，何不言？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Slanderous ministers harmed you — why did you not speak?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Scheming ministers brought you down — why did you never tell me?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣不知也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your servant did not know."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Your servant knew nothing of it."

sentences.zh: 」明年，坐累杖死，天下哀之。

translations.literal: " The next year, implicated in a case he was beaten to death; all under Heaven mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: " The next year he died under the rod in a collateral punishment, and the realm mourned him.

sentences.zh: 子四人，謫瓊州，遂為瓊山人。

translations.literal: His four sons were banished to Qiongzhou and thus became men of Qiongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His four sons were exiled to Qiongzhou and became natives of Qiongshan.

sentences.zh: 孫遠，正統七年進士。

translations.literal: Sun Yuan passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuan, a jinshi of Zhengtong year 7.

sentences.zh: 景泰時，官戶部郎中。

translations.literal: In the Jingtai period he served as Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingtai he served as a director in the revenue ministry.

sentences.zh: 天順元年，擢本部右侍郎，改工部。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun he was promoted Right Vice Minister in that ministry, then changed to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun year 1 he was promoted to right vice minister of revenue, then transferred to works.

sentences.zh: 奉詔塞開封決河。

translations.literal: He received an order to block the breached Yellow River at Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to dam the breached Yellow River channel at Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 還，仍改戶部。

translations.literal: On return he was again changed to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he moved back to revenue.

sentences.zh: 成化初，督兩廣軍餉，位至南京兵部尚書，以忤汪直免官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua he supervised military provisions in the Two Guangs, rose to Minister of War at Nanjing, and because he offended Wang Zhi was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua he oversaw army supplies in Guangdong and Guangxi, rose to Nanjing minister of war, and lost his post for crossing Wang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 其繼祥為工部尚書有名者，有秦逵等。

translations.literal: Those who succeeded Xiang as famous Ministers of Works included Qin Kui and others.
translations.idiomatic: Notable successors to Xiang as minister of works included Qin Kui and others.

sentences.zh: 逵，字文用，宣城人。

translations.literal: Kui, style name Wenyong, was a man of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kui (Wenyong) was from Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 洪武十八年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the eighteenth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Hongwu year 18.

sentences.zh: 曆事都察院。

translations.literal: He passed through service in the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 奉檄清理囚徒，寬嚴得宜。

translations.literal: Receiving a commission he cleared and reviewed prisoners; leniency and severity were fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioned to review prisoners, he balanced mercy and severity aptly.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其能，擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his ability and promoted him Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his competence and made him vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 時營繕事繁，部中缺尚書，凡興作事皆逵領之。

translations.literal: At the time construction and repair affairs were numerous; the ministry lacked a minister, and every building project Kui led.
translations.idiomatic: Construction was heavy and the ministry had no minister, so Kui headed every project.

sentences.zh: 初，議籍四方工匠，驗其丁力，定三年為班，更番赴京，三月交代，名曰「輸班匠」。

translations.literal: At first it was proposed to register artisans from the four directions, verify their labor power, fix three years as one shift, rotate in turn to the capital, hand over every three months, and call them "rotating-shift artisans."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier planners had proposed registering artisans empire-wide, gauging their strength, and sending them to the capital in three-year rotations with quarterly handovers — the "rotating shift artisans."

sentences.zh: 未及行，至是逵議量地遠近為班次，置籍，為勘合付之，至期齎至部，免其家徭役，著為令。

translations.literal: Before it could be carried out, at this time Kui proposed measuring distance near and far to set shift classes, establishing registers, issuing verification tallies, and when the term arrived bringing them to the ministry, exempting their households from corvée — enacted as an ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: The plan had not yet taken effect when Kui devised shifts by distance, issued registers and travel tallies, required artisans to report on schedule, exempted their households from corvée, and had the rule codified.

sentences.zh: 帝念逵勤勩，詔有司復其家。

translations.literal: The Emperor mindful of Kui's diligence and toil, ordered the responsible offices to restore his household.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Kui's tireless service, the emperor ordered officials to restore his family's standing.

sentences.zh: 二十二年進尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was advanced to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 明年改兵部。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he moved to the war ministry.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復改工部。

translations.literal: Before long he was again changed to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned to works.

sentences.zh: 帝以學校為國儲材，而士子巾服無異胥吏，宜更易之。

translations.literal: The Emperor took schools as the state's storehouse of talent, yet scholars' caps and robes were no different from clerks' — they should be changed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that schools stocked the state with talent, yet students dressed like clerks and ought to have distinct robes.

sentences.zh: 命逵制式以進。

translations.literal: He ordered Kui to devise a pattern and present it.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Kui to design a pattern and submit it.

sentences.zh: 凡三易，其制始定。

translations.literal: Altogether it was changed three times before the system was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: After three revisions the design was settled.

sentences.zh: 賜監生藍衫、絛各一，以為天下先。

translations.literal: He granted each student of the Directorate blue gowns and sashes, one each, to be the model for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Each student of the Directorate received a blue gown and sash as the empire's model.

sentences.zh: 明代士子衣冠，蓋創自逵雲。

translations.literal: Ming scholars' caps and robes were, it is said, first created by Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Ming scholarly dress, it is said, began with Kui.

sentences.zh: 有趙翥者，永寧人。

translations.literal: There was Zhao Zhu, a man of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhao Zhu of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 有志節，以學行聞。

translations.literal: He had will and integrity and was known for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: A man of principle, he was known for scholarship and integrity.

sentences.zh: 由訓導舉賢良，擢贊善大夫，拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: From Instructor he was raised as Worthy and Good, promoted Honorary Grand Master of the Heir Apparent, and appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from instructor through the Worthy and Good selection, he became honorary grand master of the heir apparent and then minister of works.

sentences.zh: 奏定天下歲造軍器之數，及議定籓王宮城制度。

translations.literal: He memorialized to fix the empire's yearly manufacture of military weapons, and deliberated to set princely palace-city systems.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed annual quotas for weapons empire-wide and helped set regulations for princely palaces.

sentences.zh: 趙俊者，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Zhao Jun — no one knows from what place he came.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jun was a man of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 自工部侍郎進尚書。

translations.literal: From Vice Minister of Works he was advanced to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from vice minister of works to minister.

sentences.zh: 帝以國子監所藏書板，歲久殘剝，命諸儒考補，工部督匠修治。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because printing blocks stored in the Directorate of Education over years had worn and peeled, ordered the scholars to examine and repair them, and the Ministry of Works supervised artisans in restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the Directorate of Education's printing blocks worn with age, the emperor had scholars collate the texts while the works ministry supervised craftsmen in repair.

sentences.zh: 俊奉詔監理，古籍始備。

translations.literal: Jun received the order to oversee the work; ancient books were then complete.
translations.idiomatic: Jun directed the project by imperial order, and the classical canon was restored.

sentences.zh: 洪武十二年，翥改署刑部。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongwu Zhu was changed to act in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 12 Zhu was transferred to act as minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 尋致仕去。

translations.literal: Soon he retired from service and left.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired.

sentences.zh: 俊，十七年免。

translations.literal: Jun, in the seventeenth year, was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was dismissed in year 17.

sentences.zh: 而逵於二十五年九月坐事自殺。

translations.literal: But Kui in the ninth month of the twenty-fifth year, implicated in an affair, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Kui, implicated in a case, took his own life in the ninth month of year 25.

sentences.zh: 唐鐸，字振之，虹人。

translations.literal: Tang Duo, style name Zhenzhi, was a man of Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Duo (Zhenzhi) was a native of Hong county.

sentences.zh: 太祖初起兵，即侍左右。

translations.literal: When the Taizu first raised troops, he at once attended at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu first raised his army, Duo attended him closely.

sentences.zh: 守濠州，從定江州，授西安縣丞。

translations.literal: He guarded Hao Prefecture, followed in pacifying Jiang Prefecture, and was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Xi'an County.
translations.idiomatic: He helped hold Hao Prefecture, followed the conquest of Jiangzhou, and was made assistant magistrate of Xi'an county.

sentences.zh: 召為中書省管勾。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Controller of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was called up as a controller in the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，湯和克延平，以鐸知府事，拊輯新附，士民安之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu, when Tang He took Yanping, Duo was made to administer the prefecture; he soothed and gathered the newly submitted, and gentry and people were settled.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 1, after Tang He took Yanping, Duo was named prefect and won over the newly submitted population until gentry and commoners alike were at ease.

sentences.zh: 居三年，入為殿中侍御史，復出知紹興府。

translations.literal: After three years in office he entered as Attending Censor within the Hall, then went out again to govern Shaoxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he entered court as an attending censor, then went out again as prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 六年十二月，召拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year 6 he was summoned and made minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 明年改太常卿。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became director of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，特給半俸。

translations.literal: In mourning for his mother, he was specially granted half salary.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his mother he was granted half pay by special favor.

sentences.zh: 十四年，服闋，起兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when mourning ended, he was raised as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended in year 14 he was appointed minister of war.

sentences.zh: 明年，初置諫院，以為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Remonstrance Bureau was first established, he was made Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the remonstrance bureau was first established, he was made remonstrance grand master.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗與侍臣論歷代興廢，曰：「使朕子孫如成、康，輔弼如周、召，則可祈天永命。

translations.literal: The Emperor once discussed with attending ministers the rise and fall of successive ages, saying: "If my sons and grandsons were like Cheng and Kang, and assisting ministers like the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao, then one could pray Heaven for enduring mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once discussed with his close advisers how dynasties rose and fell, saying, "If my heirs were like Kings Cheng and Kang, with helpers like the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao, we could pray Heaven for a lasting mandate.

sentences.zh: 」鐸因進曰：「豫教元良，選左右為輔導，宗社萬年福也。

translations.literal: " Duo thereupon advanced and said: "To instruct the heir in advance, to choose those at left and right as guides — that is ten-thousand-year fortune for the altars of state and grain.
translations.idiomatic: " Duo stepped forward and said, "To educate the heir early and choose upright tutors at his side is the surest blessing for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 」帝又謂鐸曰：「人有公私，故言有邪正。

translations.literal: " The Emperor again said to Duo: "People have public and private motives, therefore words have crooked and straight.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then told Duo, "Men act from public or private motives, and speech follows — straight counsel or crooked.

sentences.zh: 正言務規諫，邪言務謗諛。

translations.literal: Straight words aim at admonition and remonstrance; crooked words aim at slander and flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Honest words aim to admonish; crooked words aim to slander or flatter.

sentences.zh: 」鐸曰：「謗近忠，諛近愛。

translations.literal: " Duo said: "Slander is close to loyalty; flattery is close to affection.
translations.idiomatic: " Duo replied, "Slander wears the mask of loyalty; flattery wears the mask of affection.

sentences.zh: 不為所眩，則讒佞自遠。

translations.literal: If one is not dazzled by them, then slanderous and fawning men will themselves keep far.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty is not taken in, slanderers and flatterers will keep their distance.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，左遷監察御史。

translations.literal: " Before long he was demoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was demoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 請選賢能京官遍曆郡縣，訪求賢才，體察官吏。

translations.literal: He requested selecting worthy and able capital officials to tour all commanderies and counties, seeking worthy talent and examining officials.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed sending able capital officials through every prefecture and county to seek talent and assess local officers.

sentences.zh: 選歷練老成、望隆名重者，居布政、按察之職。

translations.literal: Choose those seasoned and mature in experience, of lofty reputation and weighty name, to hold pacification and surveillance posts.
translations.idiomatic: Veterans of proven judgment and high standing, he urged, should fill the provincial administration and surveillance posts.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 既復擢為右副都御史，曆刑、兵二部尚書。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was again promoted Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and passed through the two ministries of Punishments and War as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted again to right vice censor-in-chief and served in turn as minister of punishments and of war.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，置詹事院，命吏部曰：「輔導太子，必擇端重之士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the Household of the Heir Apparent was established; he ordered the Ministry of Personnel: "To assist and guide the Crown Prince, one must choose upright and weighty gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 the heir apparent's household was established, and he told the Ministry of Personnel, "Tutors for the crown prince must be men of sober character.

sentences.zh: 三代保傅，禮甚尊嚴。

translations.literal: The Three Dynasties' protectors and tutors — their ritual was very solemn.
translations.idiomatic: In the three ancient dynasties the guardian and tutor were honored with the highest ritual.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書鐸，謹厚有德量，以為詹事。

translations.literal: Minister of War Tang Duo is careful, generous, and has moral weight — make him Household Head.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Tang Duo is prudent, steadfast, and morally weighty — appoint him household head.

sentences.zh: 食尚書俸如故。

translations.literal: Let him receive Minister's salary as before.
translations.idiomatic: He shall keep his minister's salary unchanged.

sentences.zh: 」以鐸嘗請豫教故也。

translations.literal: " This was because Duo had once requested advance instruction.
translations.idiomatic: " This was because Duo had urged early education for the heir.

sentences.zh: 其年，致仕。

translations.literal: In that year he retired from service.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he retired.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，起太子賓客，進太子少保。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was raised as Guest of the Crown Prince and advanced to Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 he was recalled as guest of the crown prince and promoted to junior guardian of the heir.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，龍州土官趙宗壽以奏鄭國公常茂死事不實，被召，又不至。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, Longzhou native-official Zhao Zongshou, because he memorialized that Duke of Zheng Guo Chang Mao's death in service was untrue, was summoned yet did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 the Longzhou native official Zhao Zongshou reported that Duke of Zheng Guo Chang Mao's account of dying in service was false; summoned to court, he did not appear.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命楊文統大軍往討。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and ordered Yang Wen to command a great army to go punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered Yang Wen to lead a large force against him.

sentences.zh: 而命鐸招諭。

translations.literal: And he ordered Duo to summon and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Duo to go and win them over by persuasion.

sentences.zh: 鐸至，廉得茂實病死，宗壽亦伏罪來朝。

translations.literal: When Duo arrived, on discreet investigation he learned Mao had in truth died of illness; Zongshou also confessed guilt and came to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Duo arrived, his investigation showed Mao had indeed died of illness, and Zongshou confessed and came to court.

sentences.zh: 乃詔文移兵征奉議諸州叛蠻，即以鐸參議軍事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Wen to shift troops to campaign against rebellious barbarians in Fengyi and related prefectures, and at once made Duo adviser on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Wen to turn his army against the rebel tribes in Fengyi and neighboring prefectures and made Duo a military adviser.

sentences.zh: 逾月，諸蠻平。

translations.literal: After more than a month, all the barbarians were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the tribes were pacified.

sentences.zh: 鐸相度形勢，請設奉議衛及向武、河池、懷集、武仙、賀縣諸處守禦千戶所，鎮以官軍。

translations.literal: Duo surveyed the terrain and requested establishment of Fengyi Guard and garrison battalions at Xiangwu, Hechi, Huaiji, Wuxian, Hexian, and elsewhere, garrisoned with regular troops.
translations.idiomatic: Duo surveyed the terrain and proposed Fengyi Guard plus garrison battalions at Xiangwu, Hechi, Huaiji, Wuxian, Hexian, and other points, each held by regular troops.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were reported approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 鐸為人長者，性慎密，不妄取予。

translations.literal: Duo as a man was mature in bearing, by nature cautious and close, not rash in taking or giving.
translations.idiomatic: Duo was a man of steady character, cautious and discreet, never grasping or giving lightly.

sentences.zh: 帝以故舊遇之，嘗曰：「鐸自友及臣至今三十餘年，其與人交不至變色，絕亦不出惡聲。

translations.literal: The Emperor treated him as an old companion, once saying: "From friend to subject, Duo has been with me more than thirty years; in dealings with others he never shows a change of countenance, and even in severing ties he utters no harsh word.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated him as an old friend and once said, "From companion to subject, Duo has been with me more than thirty years. In all his dealings he never changes expression, and even when he breaks with someone he speaks no ill word.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「都御史詹徽剛斷嫉惡，胥吏不得肆其貪，謗訕滿朝。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Censor-in-chief Zhan Hui is stern and fair, hating evil; clerks could not indulge their greed — yet slander filled the court.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Censor-in-chief Zhan Hui is stern and hates evil, so clerks cannot indulge their greed — yet slander fills the court.

sentences.zh: 唐鐸重厚，又謂懦而無為。

translations.literal: Tang Duo is weighty and generous, yet they call him timid and inactive.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Duo is steadfast and generous, yet they call him timid and useless.

sentences.zh: 人心不古，有若是耶！

translations.literal: Human hearts are not as of old — can such things be!
translations.idiomatic: Hearts are not what they were in antiquity — can it really be so!

sentences.zh: 」後徽卒坐罪誅死，而鐸恩遇不替。

translations.literal: " Later Hui in the end was executed for a crime, yet Duo's favored treatment never diminished.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Hui was executed for a crime, yet Duo's favor at court never waned.

sentences.zh: 三十年七月，卒于京師，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the thirtieth year he died in the capital at age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the capital in the seventh month of year 30, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 賻贈甚厚，命有司護其喪歸葬。

translations.literal: Funeral gifts and posthumous grants were very lavish; he ordered the relevant offices to escort the coffin home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral gifts and posthumous honors were lavish, and he ordered the authorities to escort the coffin home for burial.

sentences.zh: 沈溍，字尚賢，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Shen Yin, style name Shangxian, was a man of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yin (Shangxian) was a native of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 與鐸同官兵部，以明敏稱。

translations.literal: He served with Duo in the Ministry of War and was known for clarity and keenness.
translations.idiomatic: He served with Duo in the Ministry of War and was famed for clarity and quick judgment.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗以勳臣子弟多骫法，撰《大誥》二十二篇，諭天下武臣，皆令誦習，使知儆惕。

translations.literal: The Emperor once, because sons of meritorious ministers often bent the law, composed twenty-two chapters of the Great Admonitions, instructing military officers throughout the realm, all ordered to recite and study so they would know awe and caution.
translations.idiomatic: Because sons of meritorious ministers so often bent the law, the emperor composed twenty-two chapters of the Great Admonitions to instruct military officers empire-wide, ordering them all to recite and study until they knew fear and restraint.

sentences.zh: 已，又以諭戒八條，頒示將士。

translations.literal: Thereafter he also issued eight admonitory precepts and displayed them to officers and troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued eight further admonitions and promulgated them to officers and troops.

sentences.zh: 時溍以試兵部侍郎掌部事，一切訓飭事宜，皆承旨行之。

translations.literal: At the time Yin, as acting Vice Minister of War managing ministry affairs, carried out all matters of instruction and discipline according to imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was then acting vice-minister of war in charge of the ministry, and every measure of discipline and instruction was carried out at the emperor's direction.

sentences.zh: 尋進尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 廣西都司建譙樓、青州衛造軍器，皆擅科民財。

translations.literal: The Guangxi military commission built a watch-tower and Qingzhou guard forged weapons — both on their own authority levied the people's wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangxi regional command built a watch-tower and Qingzhou guard forged arms, each levying civilian funds on its own authority.

sentences.zh: 溍請凡都司衛所營作，必都督府奏准。

translations.literal: Yin requested that for all construction by guards and battalions, the regional military commission must memorialize for approval.
translations.idiomatic: Yin proposed that any project by a guard or battalion must be approved by memorial through the regional command.

sentences.zh: 官給物料，毋擅役民。

translations.literal: The state was to supply materials; they must not on their own press the people for labor.
translations.idiomatic: Materials were to come from the state, and they must not press civilians into service without authority.

sentences.zh: 違者治罪。

translations.literal: Violators were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Violators were to be punished.

sentences.zh: 仍禁武臣預民事。

translations.literal: He also forbade military officers from intervening in civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also barred military officers from meddling in civil administration.

sentences.zh: 時干戈甫息，武臣暴橫，數扞文法，至是始戢，溍力也。

translations.literal: At the time weapons of war had just ceased; martial officers were violent and overbearing, often defying civil law — from this point they began to restrain themselves, largely through Yin's effort.
translations.idiomatic: The wars had only just ended; martial officers were brutal and often defied civil law. From this time they began to restrain themselves — largely through Yin's effort.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗諭致治之要在進賢、退不肖。

translations.literal: The Emperor once instructed that the key to bringing order lies in advancing the worthy and removing the unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once taught that good government depends on promoting the worthy and removing the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 溍因言：「君子常少，小人常多，在上風厲之耳，賢者舉而不仁者遠矣。

translations.literal: Yin thereupon said: "Gentlemen are always few and petty men always many; at the top one need only whip the wind — when the worthy are raised, the unkind keep far away.
translations.idiomatic: Yin replied, "Gentlemen are always few and petty men always many; what matters is the wind set at the top — raise the worthy and the unkind will keep their distance.

sentences.zh: 」帝善其言。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his words.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以溍與工部尚書秦逵換官，賜誥獎諭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Yin and Minister of Works Qin Kui exchanged posts, and edicts of commendation were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 he and Minister of Works Qin Kui exchanged posts, and both received edicts of commendation.

sentences.zh: 尋復舊任，後以事免。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to his former post; later he was dismissed for an affair.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to his former post, but was later dismissed over an affair.

sentences.zh: 明初，衛所世籍及軍卒勾補之法，皆溍所定。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ming, the hereditary registers of guards and battalions and the method of conscripting replacements for soldiers — all were set by Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, the hereditary registers of guards and battalions and the rules for replacing soldiers were all Yin's work.

sentences.zh: 然名目瑣細，簿籍煩多，吏易為奸。

translations.literal: Yet the designations were minute and the ledgers numerous; clerks easily committed fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the categories were minute and the ledgers endless, so clerks found it easy to cheat.

sentences.zh: 終明之世頗為民患，而軍衛亦日益耗減。

translations.literal: Throughout the Ming dynasty this was much a plague on the people, while the military guards also dwindled day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Through the whole Ming period it plagued the people, while the guards and battalions themselves steadily dwindled.

sentences.zh: 語詳《兵志》。

translations.literal: The matter is detailed in the Military Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The subject is treated fully in the Military Treatise.

sentences.zh: 潮州生陳質，父在戍籍。

translations.literal: Chen Zhi, a student of Chaozhou, had a father on the garrison register.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhi, a student from Chaozhou, had a father on the garrison rolls.

sentences.zh: 父沒，質被勾補，請歸卒業。

translations.literal: When the father died, Zhi was to be conscripted in his stead; he asked to return and complete his studies.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, Zhi was called up to fill the slot and asked to go home and finish his degree.

sentences.zh: 帝命除其籍。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered removal from the register.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his name struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 溍以缺軍伍，持不可。

translations.literal: Yin, because the guard corps would be short, held that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yin objected that the unit would be short a man and would not agree.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「國家得一卒易，得一士難。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "For the state to gain one soldier is easy; to gain one scholar is hard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "For the state to gain one soldier is easy; to gain one scholar is hard.

sentences.zh: 」遂除之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the removal was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The exemption was granted.

sentences.zh: 然此皆特恩雲。

translations.literal: Yet these were all special grace alone.
translations.idiomatic: But these were all special favors.

sentences.zh: 開濟，字來學，洛陽人。

translations.literal: Kai Ji, style name Laixue, was a man of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kai Ji (Laixue) was a native of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 元末為察罕帖木兒掌書記。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuan he was secretary to Chaghan Temür.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan he served as secretary to Chaghan Temür.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，以明經舉。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Hongwu he was raised on classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongwu he was recommended for mastery of the classics.

sentences.zh: 授河南府訓導，入為國子助教。

translations.literal: Appointed instructor of Henan prefecture, he entered as assistant instructor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was made instructor of Henan prefecture, then entered court as an assistant instructor at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 以疾罷歸。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him to resign and return home.

sentences.zh: 十五年七月，御史大夫安然薦濟有吏治才，召試刑部尚書，逾年實授。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifteenth year, Chief Censor An Ran recommended Ji for talent in administration of affairs; he was summoned to test as Minister of Punishments, and after more than a year received the actual appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 15 Chief Censor An Ran recommended Ji for administrative talent; summoned to trial appointment as minister of punishments, he received the full post a year later.

sentences.zh: 濟以綜核為己任，請天下諸司設文簿，日書所行事，課得失。

translations.literal: Ji took comprehensive verification as his charge; he requested that all offices throughout the realm keep ledgers, day by day writing what they did, assessing success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: Ji made thorough audit his mission and required every office to keep a daily ledger of its actions, graded for success or failure.

sentences.zh: 又各部勘合文移，立程限，定功罪。

translations.literal: He also set deadlines and rewards and punishments for joint documents transferred among ministries.
translations.idiomatic: He set deadlines and rewards and penalties for inter-ministry correspondence bearing joint seals.

sentences.zh: 又言，軍民以細故犯罪者，宜即決遣。

translations.literal: He further said that soldiers and civilians guilty of minor offenses should be decided and dispatched at once.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that soldiers and civilians guilty of petty offenses be judged and disposed of on the spot.

sentences.zh: 數月間，滯牘一清。

translations.literal: Within a few months, backlog cases were entirely cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Within months the backlog was cleared.

sentences.zh: 帝大以為能。

translations.literal: The Emperor greatly regarded him as capable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought him highly capable.

sentences.zh: 會都御史趙仁言，曩者以「賢良方正」、「孝弟力田」諸科所取士列置郡縣，多不舉職。

translations.literal: When Censor-in-chief Zhao Ren spoke, saying that those selected through the "worthy and upright," "filial and frugal, diligent in farming," and similar examinations and placed in commanderies and counties mostly did not perform their duties.
translations.idiomatic: When censor-in-chief Zhao Ren reported that men chosen through the Worthy and Upright, Filial and Frugal, Diligent in Farming, and similar examinations and posted to prefectures and counties often failed in office.

sentences.zh: 宜核其去留。

translations.literal: Their retention or removal should be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Their retention or dismissal should be reviewed.

sentences.zh: 濟條議，以「經明行修」為一科、「工習文詞」為一科、「通曉書義」為一科、「人品俊秀」為一科、「練達治理」為一科、「言有條理」為一科。

translations.literal: Ji laid out a proposal with "classics clear and conduct cultivated" as one category, "skilled in literary composition" as one, "thorough in written meaning" as one, "character handsome and outstanding" as one, "seasoned in governance" as one, "speech orderly" as one.
translations.idiomatic: Ji drafted categories: Classics Clear and Conduct Cultivated; Skilled in Literary Composition; Thorough in Written Meaning; Character Outstanding; Seasoned in Governance; and Speech Orderly.

sentences.zh: 六科備者為「上」；

translations.literal: Those complete in all six categories were "upper";
translations.idiomatic: Those who met all six were rated upper;

sentences.zh: 三科以上為「中」；

translations.literal: three categories or more were "middle";
translations.idiomatic: three or more, middle;

sentences.zh: 不及三科者為「下」。

translations.literal: fewer than three categories were "lower."
translations.idiomatic: fewer than three, lower.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 濟敏慧有才辯。

translations.literal: Ji was sharp-witted, clever, and eloquent in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was quick-witted, clever, and sharp in debate.

sentences.zh: 凡國家經制、田賦、獄訟、工役、河渠事，眾莫能裁定，濟一算畫，即有條理品式，可為世守。

translations.literal: For all matters of state institutions, land tax, lawsuits, labor service, and waterways, when none could settle them, Ji with one reckoning would produce clear regulations and forms that could be followed for generations.
translations.idiomatic: On institutions, land tax, lawsuits, labor service, and waterways — matters no one else could settle — a single calculation from Ji would yield clear rules and forms fit to last for generations.

sentences.zh: 以故帝甚信任，數備顧問，兼預他部事。

translations.literal: Therefore the Emperor trusted him deeply, often kept him for consultation, and had him participate in other ministries' affairs as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted him deeply, often kept him close for counsel, and had him weigh in on other ministries as well.

sentences.zh: 人以是忌之，謗議滋起。

translations.literal: People for this reason were jealous of him; slander and criticism mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Others resented him for it, and slander spread.

sentences.zh: 然濟亦深刻，好以法中傷人。

translations.literal: Yet Ji was also harsh and deep, fond of using the law to harm others.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ji was also harsh and loved to use the law to wound others.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉命定詐偽律。

translations.literal: He once received orders to fix the statutes on fraud.
translations.idiomatic: He was once ordered to draft the statutes on fraud.

sentences.zh: 濟議法巧密。

translations.literal: Ji's proposed law was artful and close-meshed.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's draft was artful and tight-meshed.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：：「張密網以羅民，可乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "To stretch a tight net to catch the people — can that be right?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "To stretch a tight net to catch the people — is that acceptable?

sentences.zh: 」又設籍曰「寅戌之書」，以程僚屬出入。

translations.literal: " He also set up a register called the "Book of Yin and Xu," to schedule subordinates' comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: " He also set up a register called the Book of Yin and Xu to time his subordinates' comings and goings.

sentences.zh: 帝切責曰：「古人以卯酉為常。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked him sharply, saying: "The ancients took mao and you as the norm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him sharply: "The ancients took mao and you as the norm.

sentences.zh: 今使趨事者朝寅暮戌。

translations.literal: Now you make those who hurry affairs out by yin in the morning and in by xu at night.
translations.idiomatic: Now you make men who hurry affairs leave at yin in the morning and return at xu at night.

sentences.zh: 奉父母，會妻子，幾何時耶！

translations.literal: To serve parents and meet wife and children — how much time is there!
translations.idiomatic: When can they serve their parents or see their wives and children!

sentences.zh: 」又為榜戒其僚屬，請揭文華殿。

translations.literal: " He also made a placard warning his subordinates and asked to post it in the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: " He also drafted a warning placard for his staff and asked to post it in the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「告誡僚屬之言，欲張殿廷，豈人臣禮？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Words of warning to subordinates — you wish to display them in the palace hall; is that a minister's propriety?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A minister's words of warning to his staff — and you want them hung in the palace hall? Is that proper for a subject?

sentences.zh: 」濟慚謝。

translations.literal: " Ji apologized in shame.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 尋令郎中仇衍脫囚死，為獄官所發。

translations.literal: Before long he ordered Bureau Director Qiu Yan to release a prisoner to death; this was exposed by a prison officer.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he ordered Bureau Director Qiu Yan to let a prisoner escape to his death; a prison officer exposed it.

sentences.zh: 濟與侍郎王希哲、主事王叔徵執獄官，斃之。

translations.literal: Ji, together with Vice Minister Wang Xizhe and Section Director Wang Shuzheng, seized the prison officer and beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, Vice Minister Wang Xizhe, and Section Director Wang Shuzheng seized the officer and beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，御史陶垕仲等發其事，且言：「濟奏事時，置奏答刂懷中，或隱而不言，覘伺上意，務為兩端，奸狡莫測。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year, Censor Tao Houzhong and others exposed the matter and further said: "When Ji reported affairs he kept memorial slips in his bosom, or concealed them and did not speak, watching the Emperor's intent and striving to be of two minds — crafty beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: That twelfth month Censor Tao Houzhong and others exposed the affair and added, "When Ji reported to the throne he kept memorial slips in his bosom, or held back what he knew, watching the emperor's mood and playing both sides — crafty beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 役甥女為婢。

translations.literal: He made his niece a maidservant.
translations.idiomatic: He forced his niece to serve as a maid.

sentences.zh: 妹早寡，逐其姑而略其家財。

translations.literal: His sister was widowed early; he drove out her mother-in-law and seized the family property.
translations.idiomatic: His sister was widowed young; he drove out her mother-in-law and seized the family property.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，下濟獄，並希哲、衍等皆棄市。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was furious, threw Ji into prison, and Wang Xizhe, Yan, and the rest were all executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was furious, threw Ji into prison, and Xizhe, Yan, and the rest were executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：六部之制仿于《周官》，所以佐王理邦國，熙庶績，任至重也。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: The Six Ministries system was modeled on the Offices of Zhou, to assist the king in governing the state and brightening the multitude of achievements — the charge is very heavy.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: The Six Ministries were modeled on the Offices of Zhou to help the ruler govern the realm and brighten the people's achievements — a charge of the utmost weight.

sentences.zh: 明興，建官分職，立法秩然。

translations.literal: When Ming rose, offices were established and duties divided; laws were set in clear ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming rose, offices were founded, duties divided, and laws set in clear order.

sentences.zh: 又三途用人，求賢彌廣。

translations.literal: They also used three paths to employ men, seeking worthies ever more broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Three paths of recruitment widened the search for talent still further.

sentences.zh: 若陳修、滕毅之典銓法，楊思義、範敏之治賦役，周禎之定律令，單安仁之領將作，以至沈溍、開濟輩之所經畫，皆委曲詳備，細大不遺。

translations.literal: From Chen Xiu and Teng Yi's directing the selection law, Yang Siyi and Fan Min's administering tax and corvée, Zhou Zhen's fixing statutes, Dan Anren's heading the Directorate of Works, down to the plans of Shen Yin, Kai Ji, and their like — all were tortuously thorough, omitting nothing small or large.
translations.idiomatic: From Chen Xiu and Teng Yi directing selection, Yang Siyi and Fan Min administering tax and corvée, Zhou Zhen fixing statutes, and Dan Anren heading the Directorate of Works, down to the schemes of Shen Yin, Kai Ji, and their peers — all were thorough in every twist, omitting nothing great or small.

sentences.zh: 考其規模，固一代政治之權輿者歟。

translations.literal: Considering their scale, they were indeed the wagon-shaft of dynastic government in their age.
translations.idiomatic: Measured by their scope, they were indeed the foundation of that generation's government.
